_schema_notes.purpose: Worked example for pipeline_report.py. Every name here is invented. The routine writes a file in exactly this shape each run.
_schema_notes.sev: One of crit (Quiet & stuck: tiers 1-2), warn (Blocked: tiers 3-5), note (Analysis gap: tiers 6-7), info (Data cleanup: tier 8), ok (On track).
_schema_notes.quiet: Whole days since the last client email (0 = today). null when no client email was found in 60 days.
_schema_notes.last.dir: SENT TO (team emailed the client; team = who sent it) or FROM (client emailed us; team = who received it).
_schema_notes.flags: Each flag is {k, text} or {k, carriers:[{name, days, open}]}. open:false shows a carrier greyed (e.g. only 2 days out). Keys used: Quotes, Outstanding, Not sent, Census, Analysis, Selector, Drift, Data, Open question, Context, Misfiled, Setup, Status, Sensitive, Ready.
_schema_notes.grid: Values: 'y' = check, 'y:extra' = check plus a short note (e.g. 'y:nov2026'), 'n' = cross, '—' = not applicable, anything else is shown in amber (partial, stale, cold, archived). sent/received/outstanding are short text like '6/6'.
_schema_notes.markup: Text fields may use **bold**, *italic* and `mono` (for file names). Nothing else; no HTML.
_schema_notes.never: No SSNs, tax IDs, dates of birth or member IDs anywhere in this file.
